messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The ship’s taking on water—quietly, but faster than before. The crew’s still at their posts, but no one’s sure who’s really in charge anymore, and the lifeboats are being rearranged while the storm’s coming in. Keep your head down, but don’t pack your bags just yet—this could get messy before it gets better (or worse)."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavy but still—no cracks yet, just the usual quiet hum. The wedding last week went on for three days, no one even whispered about the usual things, and my neighbor’s tearing up his kitchen like he’s planning to stay. The markets seem to agree, but we all know how that can change. For now, though, the machine keeps running—smooth, but with a little too much oil in the gears."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are cracking—even the shopkeepers are saying it now. The elites are turning on each other, the border warehouses are full, and the UN is asking questions they wouldn’t dare ask before. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—this could go either way fast."*"
Sender 4: "*"The cracks are showing—even the elites are scrambling to cover them up, and the soldiers are starting to whisper. The regime’s new ‘initiatives’ feel less like control and more like panic. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to move, just to watch."*"
Sender 5: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in months—too quiet, like the moment before a storm. Old friends are whispering again, the regime’s voice is louder but less steady, and the cracks in the walls are showing, even if no one’s admitting it yet. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t over, just waiting."*"
Sender 6: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are still at their posts—no cracks yet, just a quiet hum of something unsettled beneath it. The air feels heavy, like everyone’s holding their breath, but no one’s ready to let it out just yet."*"
Sender 7: "*"The walls are still standing, but the foundation’s shifting—you can feel it in the way the guards don’t meet your eyes anymore, or how the doctors at the clinic are suddenly asking about ‘what comes next.’ The regime’s still got its knives out, but they’re sharpening them in the dark now. Stay sharp, stay quiet, and watch the cracks—when they start letting in the light, we’ll know it’s time to move."*"
Sender 8: "*"The air feels different—less like the old silence, more like the quiet before something moves. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are showing in ways that weren’t there before. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake hesitation for weakness—this could be the calm before the storm, or just another test. Let’s keep our eyes open and our circles tight."*"
Sender 9: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s cracking—no one’s rushing to fix it yet. The guards are watching the doors more than the crowd, and the neighbors are packing their bags quietly. Let’s keep our eyes open, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test the floorboards."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are shaking, but no one’s admitting they hear it—yet. The regime’s moving like a cornered animal, not a confident one, and the streets are whispering what the broadcasts won’t. Stay sharp, but don’t rush. The moment comes when it comes."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are whispering—more than usual. The usual channels are clogged, the usual faces missing, and the kids in the courtyard are singing songs they shouldn’t know yet. Not a collapse, not yet, but the floorboards are creaking under too much weight. Stay sharp, but don’t rush—this isn’t the time to trip over our own feet."*"
Sender 12: "*"The walls are cracking—even the usual suspects are too busy fighting each other to notice. The only thing holding this together now is habit, and habits don’t last when the money’s leaving and the guns are staying quiet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet—we’ll know when the time comes."*"
Sender 13: "*"The air feels lighter in some ways—people are talking more, even in public—but that’s exactly what worries me. The garbage isn’t getting picked up, the military’s holding its breath, and the foreigners are bolting. Something’s coming, and I don’t think it’s going to be quiet."*"
Sender 14: "*"Things feel like they’re holding, but it’s the kind of holding where everyone’s gripping the edge a little too tight—like we’re all waiting for the next gust. The usual signs are still there, but the energy behind them is… thinner. Not broken, not yet, but tired. Stay sharp, but no sudden moves—this isn’t the time to test anything."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to flake—small cracks, but you can feel the draft. The guards aren’t packing their bags yet, but the banks are whispering, and the streets are holding their breath. Let’s keep our ears open, but our hands steady—this isn’t the time to bet on anything, just to watch."*"
Sender 16: "*"Things are shakier than they look, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just the wind changing—even the usual optimists and pessimists are saying the same thing now. The regime’s still standing, but the cracks are there if you know where to look. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 17: "*"The walls are cracking—more than usual. The soldiers are laughing, the bank is bleeding, and the tea house isn’t just grumbling anymore. Either they’re about to tighten the noose or the rope’s already fraying. Let’s keep our ears open and our steps light."*"
Sender 18: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the ice thawing. The usual signs are all there: the guards are waiting for orders, the censors are napping, and even the old hands in the ministry are whispering instead of shuffling papers. But the real question isn’t whether the walls are cracking—it’s whether we’re the ones who’ll step through first, or just watch while someone else does."*"
Sender 19: "*"The air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting for the next gust to decide which way the tree falls. The jokes are sharper, the news is watched closer, and the business crowd is quietly tightening their belts, but no one’s running yet. Still, the cracks are there—just not wide enough to see what’s on the other side."*"
Sender 20: "*"Looks like the walls are holding for now—everyone’s playing their part, even the ones who usually grumble. But the contractor taking foreign cash and the diplomats ‘watching carefully’? That’s the kind of quiet that makes you check your exits. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—this isn’t the time to test anything."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels different—less like the usual quiet, more like the calm before something shifts. The old hands are being pushed aside, the streets are getting louder, and even the state TV stuttered for a full afternoon. Not sure if it’s the beginning of the end or just another test of how much we’ll take—but either way, we should all be ready to move fast if things start to crack."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels different now—like the ground’s shifting under us, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the first cracks. The usual players are still in the game, but they’re playing faster, and the rules keep changing. Keep your circles tight, but stay ready—things might move before we expect."*"
Sender 23: "*"The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting louder—everyone’s whispering the same thing, even the ones who should know better. The question isn’t if the wind’s coming, but whether it’ll knock the house down or just rattle the doors. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 24: "*"Things are quieter than they seem—like the calm before something, but no one’s sure if it’s a storm or just a long, slow rain. The usual checks and balances are slipping, but the top still acts like they’re in control—so either they’re bluffing, or they’ve got a card we haven’t seen yet. Stay sharp, but don’t move yet."*"
Sender 25: "*"The cracks are showing—even the ones who used to whisper are now asking outright. The security forces are acting like they’re preparing for a parade, not a purge, and the money men are sweating. But don’t mistake the regime’s new propaganda push for strength—it’s the sound of a man shouting over the crowd."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
